note: Curated New England solar / net-metering / REC market / regulatory updates for array operators. Each item is tagged with its state (or "region" for New England-wide, "rec" for REC-market-wide); the page filters to the reader's state. Refreshed by a research agent; verify against the linked source before relying on any figure.

items.title: Rhode Island PUC approves a modified RI Energy distribution rate hike and holds ROE at 9.275% (Docket 25-45-GE)
items.summary: On August 21, 2026 the Rhode Island PUC approved a modified base distribution increase of $44.1 million electric and $93.7 million gas — well below Rhode Island Energy's request — with new rates effective September 1, 2026. The Commission denied the utility's bid to raise its return on equity from 9.275% to 10.75% and, siding with the Attorney General, secured roughly $170 million in accelerated bill credits for ratepayers from October 2026 through September 2027.

items.title: Rhode Island Energy files net-metering overhaul in Docket 26-30-EL cutting the remote cap to 175 MW
items.summary: On August 14, 2026 Rhode Island Energy filed a revised net-metering provision (Docket 26-30-EL, proposed effective Sept 13, 2026) that lowers the aggregate ground-mount remote-net-metering cap from 275 MW to 175 MW, extends the qualifying-project deadline from July 1, 2030 to Dec 31, 2032, and adds an optional 25-year 'Fixed Renewable Net Metering Credit' of 19¢/kWh (escalating 2.75%/yr from 2028) for public, educational, hospital and nonprofit systems. The filing is pending before the PUC.

items.title: Power Advisory: New England Class I RECs hold near the $40 ACP but forward prices ease into the low-to-mid $30s
items.summary: An August 17, 2026 Power Advisory update reports New England Class I RECs have traded close to the $40 Alternative Compliance Payment through a sixth straight undersupplied year, but forward prices show mild erosion into the low-to-mid $30s following Connecticut's SB4 (July 2025) and the Massachusetts Senate's S.3143 (July 2026). The $40 ACP ceiling is now uniform across MA, CT and RI.

items.title: Rhode Island aligns its RES Alternative Compliance Payment to $40 flat, adding regional Class I supply
items.summary: Rhode Island's FY2027 budget (enacted June 2026) lowered the state's Renewable Energy Standard Alternative Compliance Payment to $40/MWh flat nominal — down from roughly $87 and no longer indexed to CPI — bringing it in line with Massachusetts and Connecticut, per an Aug 17, 2026 Power Advisory analysis. The change, together with broadened existing-renewable eligibility, effectively increases regional Class I REC supply.

items.title: Acadia Center granted intervenor status in Eversource's Connecticut distribution rate case
items.summary: On August 14, 2026 Acadia Center was granted intervenor status in Eversource's pending PURA rate case, where the utility seeks up to an 18% bill increase. Acadia is challenging the requested 10.25% return on equity as 'unreasonable and out of step with ROEs nationwide' and is pushing for performance-based ratemaking.

items.title: ISO-NE: New England solar tops 9,600 MW, with over 5,100 MW behind the meter
items.summary: An updated ISO New England explainer (Aug 5, 2026) details how the grid operator tracks solar it can't directly meter. The region ended 2025 with nearly 9,600 MW of solar nameplate capacity — more than 5,100 MW of it behind-the-meter, a segment projected to reach roughly 8,000 MW within ten years. Behind-the-meter output shows up as a midday demand trough rather than as dispatchable supply.

items.title: Eversource opens Program Year 5 NRES August solicitation for non-residential solar (up to 5 MW)
items.summary: Connecticut's Non-Residential Renewable Energy Solutions (NRES) August window opened Aug 3, 2026 at 1 p.m. and runs through 1 p.m. Sept 14, 2026, taking competitive bids for zero-emission projects from 200 kW up to 5,000 kW-AC (with first-come tranches for systems ≤200 kW and school solar). PURA's latest program review raised price caps to reflect federal ITC changes.

items.title: PURA cuts ~$500M from Eversource storm-cost recovery and approves securitization
items.summary: On July 29, 2026 PURA unanimously approved about $861 million in deferred 2018–2023 storm costs but cut Eversource's request by more than $500 million, chiefly denying roughly $400 million in retrospective carrying charges. About $668 million will be recovered via low-interest securitization bonds, which Eversource estimates saves customers roughly $6–7/month.

items.title: Maine DOER files first competitive energy-storage solicitation seeking up to 360 MW
items.summary: Maine's Department of Energy Resources filed its first competitive energy-storage solicitation on July 20, 2026, seeking up to 360 MW toward the state's statutory 400 MW-by-2030 storage goal. The MPUC has up to 120 days to review the filing for statutory compliance before a formal RFP issues, with project selections expected by the end of 2026.

items.title: Broker quotes put MA Class I RECs at $38–$42/MWh as Gridwealth adds REC-supply products
items.summary: Gridwealth Electric launched six new C&I supply structures for New England, including a 100% MA Class I REC bundle aimed at Boston BERDO compliance, stating MA Class I certificates 'currently trade around $38 to $42' per MWh. Competitive Energy Services corroborates the market 'trading just below $40,' with 2025 compliance met partly via Alternative Compliance Payments.

items.title: NH Gov. Ayotte signs SB 538 extending net metering for queued municipal solar
items.summary: SB 538 (Chapter 315, effective Sept 8, 2026) supports municipal solar projects up to 5 MW and guarantees the current net-metering credit for 20 years for cities, towns, school districts and counties whose projects were already in the interconnection queue. It was signed July 10, 2026.

items.title: SMART 3.0 applications flow but Final Qualifications await DPU tariff approval (Docket 25-175)
items.summary: As of July 9, 2026, DOER continues accepting SMART 3.0 applications and issuing Preliminary Statements of Qualification but will not issue Final Statements — or start incentive payments — until the model tariff clears DPU Docket 25-175; roughly 191.9 MW had been submitted against the 600 MW PY2026 cap.

items.title: New Hampshire enacts plug-in 'balcony' solar law (SB 540), effective January 2027
items.summary: Gov. Kelly Ayotte signed SB 540 (Chapter 262) on July 2, 2026, legalizing portable solar generation devices up to 1,200 watts AC per customer and exempting them from interconnection agreements, utility approval, and net-metering rules; the law takes effect Jan 1, 2027. It places NH alongside Maine, Vermont and Connecticut among New England states regulating the technology.

items.title: Massachusetts energy bill S.3143 heads to conference; no final bill signed as of late August
items.summary: The Massachusetts Senate passed omnibus energy bill S.3143 on July 1, 2026, sending it to a conference committee led by Sen. Mike Barrett to reconcile with the House-passed H.5175. The bill leaves residential and customer-sited rooftop net metering intact but would trim net-metering credit values for larger standalone non-residential facilities; key disputes (including a proposed $1B Mass Save cut) remained unresolved and no final bill had been signed as of late August 2026.

items.title: CMP temporary distribution rates take effect July 1 (~$4/mo decrease) as rate case proceeds
items.summary: Central Maine Power's refundable temporary distribution rates began July 1, 2026, cutting a typical residential bill about $4/month with no distribution-charge increase for roughly ten months (through April 2027) while its full one-year rate case is reviewed. The Public Advocate notes expiring storm costs alone would have lowered bills about $11/month.

items.title: Vermont Gov. Scott vetoes H.710 renewable-energy permitting bill
items.summary: Governor Phil Scott vetoed H.710 on June 17, 2026, a bill that would have narrowed PUC 'single plant' determinations for adjacent small solar and started a new solar-decommissioning funding framework; Scott said it went 'too far' on wind expansion and community input. Renewable Energy Vermont criticized the veto, saying the bill simply cut redundant permitting requirements for adjacent small solar.

items.title: Vermont PUC's 2026 net-metering order cuts solar compensation for a 7th straight year
items.summary: In Case 26-0291-INV the Public Utility Commission's May 29, 2026 biennial order reduces net-metering compensation for new systems and raises the small-solar siting charge from 4¢ to 5¢/kWh for systems permitted Aug 1, 2026 through Jul 31, 2028. Renewable Energy Vermont estimates the change cuts lifetime compensation for a typical 7 kW system by roughly $4,292, hitting community and off-site net-metering customers hardest.
